- **PR #221 (C11 cause and fix) merged** as `123dab63`. Linux-test-only C11 diagnostics
  located the refusal. During TLS the issuer's outbound strict-registry check of the
  learner's server certificate returned ‘founder registry unavailable’ at 3.66 ms. The
  check used a non-waiting applied-store try-lock, and transient contention was the
  leading explanation. The trace reported registry unavailability without identifying the
  specific store condition (run 44858188771, stage ‘TLS server authorization’, log
  `D:/Temp/arx-pr221-fail/ubuntu-rust.log` SHA256 `55998d64…462b`). **Owner decision
  (2026-11-21):** a narrow production fix, a short bounded wait instead of instant refusal
  on contention, keeping instant fail-closed refusal for poison, an unavailable store and
  clock failure. Final design: rustls keeps full chain, cluster and possession checks;
  strict clients authorize after TLS and before their first frame write, strict servers
  and learners before their first frame read; final dispatch and client reply validation
  recheck; each check waits at most 4 ms on Tokio timers with no guard across await. ADR
  0041 records the residual that rustls can decrypt a bounded amount of application data
  (16 KiB plaintext backpressure, record-deframer caps) before the binding check, which
  Arxcovo never parses and refusal drops. Reviews: 1 HOLD (blocking `thread::sleep` on a
  Tokio worker; `D:/Temp/arx-pr221-review/review.md`, SHA256 `d6cb99e5…3ae5`); 2 cancelled as

**Standing pre-start recovery rule (owner oversight reiterated 2026-11-19):** a
cancelled job with zero executed steps, no assigned runner and an explicit
runner-acquisition failure is retried on the unchanged head **without owner
approval**. This is infrastructure recovery, not a test rerun or a fix attempt;
exhausted fix counters do not apply. Retry only that job and its dependent gates,
retaining successful workers. If acquisition fails again, use hourly recovery,
at most four requests, with a durable request count and next action. Stop this
route if a step executed, source changed, or a genuine test failure appears.
Preserve every failed API attempt and its original budget result; never relabel
it green. Accept the recovered first actual execution only after all required
checks, exact-head independent review and current main budget gates pass. Keep
ci-time-budget/agent-review/protection, timeouts and quarantine unchanged. The
earlier demand for new approval for PR182's zero-step cancellation was incorrect
and is superseded by this standing rule (previously applied for PR163).

## Windows development execution — Opus continuation (2026-11-11)

- Provider/effort: Anthropic claude-opus-5-5, high (other-provider continuation
  under the three-failed-fixes rule). Outcome: candidate complete locally and
  pending a fresh independent Sol review. Base `8953246`, Sol candidate
  `68c6dbd`, head recorded by the coordinator at handoff. No push, PR,
  dispatch, settings, account, rights, service or task change, elevation, S4U
  probe or owner acceptance was performed. Last merged PR is unchanged by this
  work.
- Junction root cause (deterministic loop first): the failure reproduced, and
  captured stderr was `md`'s own error. cmd.exe scans its whole command line for
  switches, so the fixture's argv0 `...\System32/cmd.exe` was parsed as

The correction uses a shared atomic closed-admission bit/live-ticket count.
Foreground MCP handlers acquire a ticket before any activity access; drain closes
admission on the same atomic before observing zero. A command/discovery transfers
its ticket through the worker's terminal commit. An open-row ticket dropped on
failure latches unconfirmed completion. Read-tool terminal write failure also
requires an unconfirmed/nonzero shutdown when that foreground executor is present.
